note: Parenthesised area code. The label is the whole number including the open paren. This was the detector's single exact miss: the pattern's leading \b anchor could not match between a space and a non-word character, so the '(' was dropped and the span started one byte late (an exact FN here and an exact FP against the label). Fixed by giving the parenthesised branch of the phone pattern no leading anchor, so this case now scores exact-clean. It is the reason the two matching granularities are reported separately — overlap matching credited the near-miss and localised it to a boundary bug.

note: Regression case for the historical phone-vs-card defect. A bare 16-digit run has no non-digit boundary, so the phone recognizer's \b anchors cannot match it at all and the CARD must win. Unanchored, the phone pattern would match the first ten digits, score 0.98 against the card's 0.95, and take the span — a precision loss and a mis-typed entity. Mutation-verified: removing the \b anchors fails this case.
text: Card 4111111111111111 was charged to the account yesterday.

note: Second regression case for the phone-vs-card   defect, in a sentence where the digits are described as an opaque token. 5555555555554444 is a Luhn-VALID Mastercard, so the Luhn validator detects it and the card must win over the phone recognizer. (An earlier version of this case used 1234567890123456 and was WRONG: that number fails Luhn, so a checksum-validating detector must reject it, and the case was measuring a card that does not exist. Replaced, not relabelled, because the intent was always a valid card.)
text: The rotating token 5555555555554444 expired before the batch finished.

note: 16 digits that FAIL the Luhn checksum (verified: 4111111111111112 sums to a non-multiple of 10), so this is correctly a negative case. The detector currently REPORTS it, because NewScrubber never registers checksum.LuhnValidator and the regex card recognizer only checks length 13-19. Recorded as a known false positive rather than relabelled, because the label is right and the detector is wrong. See TODO.md.
